CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Evelyn is a 56-year-old female presenting for her annual examination. She reports that her herniated disc has been doing well since receiving a steroid injection several months ago, with no back pain or limitations in movement. She is back to work following her prior carpal tunnel release and denies any recurrent issues, numbness, or tingling in her hands. She reports good full range of motion in her wrists. Over the last month, she has been experiencing chest pain that occurs with walking and resolves with rest. She denies chest pain at rest. She describes the pain as a burning sensation located in the middle of her chest, occurring approximately three times per week. She denies associated shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting. She reports mild nasal congestion from allergies due to pollen.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for chest pain with exertion that resolves with rest and nasal congestion from allergies. Negative for shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting, lower extremity edema, muscle aches, fever, or chills.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Coronary artery disease with prior stenting
Carpal tunnel syndrome, status post release
Herniated disc

MEDICATIONS
Aspirin
Toprol

ALLERGIES
Pollen (environmental)

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is currently working

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Blood pressure well controlled, oxygen saturation normal
Heart: Slight 3/6 systolic ejection murmur
Lungs: Clear bilaterally
Carotid arteries: No bruits appreciated
Extremities: No lower extremity edema; healed surgical scars on right wrist

RESULTS
Echocardiogram (prior year): Left ventricular ejection fraction 45%, mild mitral regurgitation
EKG: Stable, reflecting prior coronary artery disease, no new changes

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Carpal tunnel syndrome, status post release: Doing well. Continue current management. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
2. Herniated disc: Responding well to prior steroid injection. No further intervention needed at this time. Patient to report if recurrent symptoms develop.
3. Coronary artery disease with recurrent chest pain: Concerning for angina. Continue aspirin and Toprol. Order cardiac stress test to evaluate for additional blockages. Order lipid panel. Start Crestor 20 mg once daily. Nurse will schedule testing and follow-up.
